fatal_errors: The proposed CoCrFeMnNi coating does not reconstruct the target FeNiCrCoCu coating.
The response replaces the target nanoindentation/friction simulations over 300–1200 K with an unspecified coating-deposition and room-temperature testing scenario.
The proposed interdiffusion zone, Cr- or Mn-rich precipitates, Mn2O3, and Orowan-strengthening mechanism are not supported by the cited evidence.
It misses the key 900 K transition from stacking-fault-mediated deformation to lattice disorder, along with the associated sharp losses in hardness and wear resistance.
The cited paper concerns bulk additively manufactured CoCrFeMnNi under compression and does not establish adhesion to Cu, coating wear behavior, or the claimed interface chemistry.
explanation: The hypothesis is aligned only at the broad level of using an FCC high-entropy-alloy coating to improve the wear resistance of copper. It does not identify the target FeNiCrCoCu material, coating geometry, crystallographic setup, molecular-dynamics intervention, or thermal conditions. Its generic prediction of improved hardness relative to bare Cu is directionally plausible, but it does not reproduce the target temperature dependence: stability through 600 K, an elastic-modulus maximum at 600 K, and sharp degradation with increased friction above 900 K. The proposed experiment could test coating performance and adhesion, but it would not discriminate the target mechanism without temperature-resolved measurements of lattice disorder, HCP fraction, dislocation line length, modulus, and friction. Most importantly, E1 does not support the interfacial or precipitation claims, so the alternative remains speculative rather than evidence-grounded.
